text:
Ava: Quick thread — thinking about adding fallback priority controls into the rollout UI for canaries/A-B tests. Goal: deterministic, auditable fallbacks for region outage, model variant failures, and capacity shortfalls. TL;DR: propose precedence + safety nets. Thoughts? :thinking:

Ravi: Configurable per-route please. Some routes can't cross-region due to data residency. also quotas need to block fallbacks that would exceed billing commitments.

Sasha: I lean towards model-variant before region to keep latency predictable, but if infra-level region failure detected we should fail over region first. Need clear health signals and priority semantics.

Ava: Good call. Two orthogonal knobs: precedence (ordered list) + constraints (allow/disallow by tag: residency, quantization, verified). UX question: expose as simple dropdown presets + advanced JSON editor?

Ava: Example policy (proposal):
```yaml
fallback_policy:
  precedence:
    - regional_failover
    - model_variant
    - capacity_bump
  constraints:
    - disallow_tags: ["unverified-weights"]
  safeguards:
    - global_error_threshold: {percent:5, window_s:30}
    - require_approval_for_unverified: true
  rollout_adjustments:
    capacity_bump: {max_percent:50, target_pool: "shared-burst"}
```

Lena: Telemetry needs: store "fallback.reason" and "fallback.path" in traces, and emit counter metrics for each type. Also add a panel showing % rollouts that triggered fallback within first 10 minutes.

Kai: Consider RBAC + billing flags: capacity_bump may consume reserved pools; we need to prevent overflow into other customers' dedicated capacity. Also ensure audit log entry for any automated fallback that moves traffic across billing tiers. :rotating_light:

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary started 10% -> redwood-canary-west (job id: canary-20260301-42)

Sasha: Test plan idea: simulated 503s at model layer to validate model_variant fallback; simulate region-level network partition to validate regional_failover; load-test capacity bump to ensure autoscaler doesn't thrash. Add chaos tests to CI.

Ava: Edge case: simultaneous region outage + model-variant throttle. Proposal: if region outage is detected by infra heartbeat, prefer regional_failover; else prefer model_variant. But add tie-breaker that avoids increasing mean latency by >50ms.

Ravi: Add global circuit-breaker: if >5% error across all variants for route over 30s, abort rollout and revert to previous stable config. Need an emergency stop API.

Lena: I'll prototype the dashboards: "Fallbacks by reason", "Avg failover latency", and a per-rollout timeline that shows when fallbacks fired. Will add quick filters for residency-tagged routes.

Kai: I'll add a new API field `fallback_policy` to rollout endpoints. Minimal schema now and we can extend. Example curl: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rollouts 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' 
  -d '{"model":"gptx-v1","canary":{"percent":10},"fallback_policy": {"precedence":["regional_failover","model_variant"]}}'
```

Sasha: Also require policy change reviews: any change that increases traffic to an unquantized/unverified variant needs two approvers and a staged rollout flag.

Ava: Agreed. Add a safeguard: policy changes that can route >20% traffic to unverified models are gated behind 2 approvals and a manual opt-in flag in the UI. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary updated -> 25% (canary-20260301-42)

Ava: Thanks all — I'll open a PR with the spec + UI mockups and link this thread. @Lena please add dashboards, @Kai will follow-up with API patch. tagging oncall FYI.
